D: A hardworking waitress in New Orleans kisses a frog prince and ends up a frog herself.
P: Serve the snacks when Tiana hands Charlotte a plate of hot beignets.
S: Fried yeast dough squares, soft and puffy
Yeasted dough rolled and cut into squares, fried at 180C until puffed and golden, buried under icing sugar and served hot.
Bayou crab cakes with Creole remoulade
Louis, Ray and the frogs in the bayou

Crab cakes bound with mayo, mustard and spring onion, fried crisp, with a punchy Creole remoulade of pickles, capers and hot sauce. Mix 400g drained crab meat with 3 tbsp mayo, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, 2 sliced spring onions, 1 egg, 60g panko and 1/2 tsp Cajun spice. Shape into 8 cakes and chill 30 minutes. Fry in oil and butter for 3 minutes a side until golden. For the remoulade, mix 120g mayo with 1 tbsp chopped pickles, 1 tbsp capers, 1 tsp mustard, 1 tsp hot sauce and paprika. Serve with lemon.
Cob loaf layered with olive salad, salami, ham and provolone
Round loaf filled with salami, ham, provolone and a chopped olive salad, pressed overnight, cut into small wedges.
M: Daddy James's chicken and sausage gumbo
the gumbo Tiana's daddy taught her, shared with the whole street

Chicken and smoky sausage in a dark, nutty roux with okra, capsicum, celery and onion, ladled over rice with spring onion and hot sauce. Stir 80ml oil and 80g plain flour in a heavy pot over medium heat for 20 minutes until dark brown. Add 1 diced onion, 1 green capsicum and 2 celery sticks and cook 5 minutes. Add 600g diced chicken thighs, 300g sliced smoked sausage, 2 tsp Cajun spice and 1.2L chicken stock. Simmer for 1 hour, adding 200g sliced okra for the last 15 minutes. Serve over 300g cooked rice with spring onion and hot sauce.
Garlic bacon prawns over cheddar polenta
Prawns sautéed with garlic, bacon and Cajun spice, spooned over creamy cheesy polenta with spring onion.
W: Bananas cooked in butter, brown sugar and cinnamon

Bananas caramelised in butter, brown sugar and cinnamon with a splash of orange, spooned hot over vanilla ice cream with toasted pecans. Melt 60g butter in a frying pan with 100g brown sugar and 1/2 tsp cinnamon and stir until bubbling. Add 4 bananas, halved lengthways and across, and cook 2 minutes a side until caramelised. Pour in the juice of 1 orange and 1 tsp vanilla and let it bubble into a glossy sauce. Spoon over scoops of vanilla ice cream and scatter with 50g toasted chopped pecans.
K: Strong chicory coffee over ice with vanilla syrup and milk

Strong coffee and chicory brew poured over ice with cold milk and vanilla sugar syrup, a New Orleans morning with beignets on the side. Brew 500ml strong coffee using 4 tbsp ground coffee and 1 tbsp roasted chicory, then cool. Simmer 60g caster sugar with 60ml water and 1 tsp vanilla to a syrup. Fill 4 glasses with ice, add 1 tbsp syrup and 150ml cold milk to each, then pour over the coffee. For the kids, make it with decaf or just chilled milk and syrup.

dishes.make_ahead: Make the dough up to 1 day ahead and prove it slowly in the fridge overnight instead of the 2 hour prove; cut, fry and dust with icing sugar just before serving

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, eggs, butter and evaporated milk with enough warm water to a soft dough.
Knead briefly until smooth.
Cover and prove until doubled.
Roll out and cut into squares.
Fry in the vegetable oil at 180C in batches until puffed and golden.
Bury under icing sugar and serve hot.

steps.text: Chop the olives and giardiniera together for an olive salad.
Hollow the loaf slightly.
Layer with olive salad, salami, ham and provolone, then more olive salad.
Wrap tightly and press under a heavy weight overnight in the fridge.
Cut into small wedges.

dishes.make_ahead: Peel the prawns and slice the spring onions up to 1 day ahead in the fridge; cook the polenta and finish the dish on the night

steps.text: Peel the prawns and prepare the spring onions.
Simmer the polenta in the water, stirring, until thick.
Beat the cheddar into the polenta.
Fry the bacon until crisp.
Add the garlic, prawns and Cajun seasoning and cook until the prawns are pink.
Spoon over the polenta and scatter with spring onion.

veg.n: Tiana's Palace Cajun mushrooms and grits
veg.make_ahead: Slice the mushrooms and spring onions up to 1 day ahead in the fridge; make the polenta and fry the mushrooms on the night

steps.text: Slice the mushrooms and spring onions.
Simmer the polenta in the water, stirring, until thick.
Beat the cheddar and butter into the polenta.
Fry the mushrooms in the oil with the smoked paprika until browned and crisp at the edges.
Add the garlic and Cajun seasoning and cook for a minute.
Spoon over the polenta and scatter with spring onion.

dishes.make_ahead: Toast the pecans up to 2 days ahead and keep airtight; the banana sauce is best cooked just before serving over the ice cream

steps.text: Toast the pecans in a dry pan.
Melt the butter in a frying pan with the brown sugar and cinnamon and stir until bubbling.
Add the bananas, halved lengthways and across, and cook until caramelised on each side.
Pour in the orange juice and vanilla and let it bubble into a glossy sauce.
Spoon over scoops of ice cream and scatter with the pecans.

dishes.make_ahead: Coffee and syrup up to 2 days, keep chilled

steps.text: Brew the coffee with the chicory in the boiling water.
Cool the coffee.
Simmer the sugar, water and vanilla to a syrup.
Fill glasses with ice, add syrup and cold milk, then pour over the coffee. For the kids, use decaf or just milk and syrup.

s.note: Fried yeast dough squares, soft and puffy
s.how: Mix 500g flour, 7g yeast, 2 eggs, 50g melted butter and 250ml evaporated milk with warm water to a soft dough and prove 2 hours. Roll out, cut into squares and fry at 180C until puffed and golden. Bury under icing sugar and serve hot.

s.note: Cob loaf layered with olive salad, salami, ham and provolone
s.how: Chop green olives and giardiniera together for an olive salad. Hollow a cob loaf slightly and layer with olive salad, salami, ham and provolone, then more olive salad. Wrap tightly, press under a heavy weight overnight and cut into small wedges.

m.note: Garlic bacon prawns over cheddar polenta
m.how: Simmer 200g polenta in 1L water, stirring, until thick, then beat in grated cheddar. Fry 150g diced bacon until crisp, add crushed garlic and 500g peeled green prawns with Cajun seasoning and cook 3 minutes. Spoon over the polenta with spring onion.
